items.q: Grandma ______ in this village since she was a little girl.
items.vi: Bà nội đã sống ở ngôi làng này từ khi còn là một cô bé.
items.explanation:
Since she was a little girl gives the starting point of an action that continues to now, so the present perfect has lived is needed.
✗ lives — present simple cannot combine with 'since' + a past point; ✗ lived — past simple would mean the living is finished, but she still lives there; ✗ is living — present continuous describes a temporary action now, not one lasting since childhood.

items.q: Although she had made lots of new friends at the summer camp, Lan still felt ______ and kept talking about her mum’s cooking and her own little bedroom.
items.vi: Dù đã có nhiều bạn mới ở trại hè, Lan vẫn thấy nhớ nhà và cứ nhắc mãi về món mẹ nấu và căn phòng nhỏ của mình.
items.explanation:
Homesick = sad because you are away from home and miss it; the clue is that she kept talking about her mum's cooking and her own little bedroom.
✗ lonely — sad because you have no company, but she had made lots of new friends; ✗ nostalgic — missing a time in the past, not a place; ✗ bored — having nothing interesting to do, which does not explain missing home.

items.q: The forecast says there will be ______ rain all weekend, so the picnic in the forest is cancelled.
items.vi: Dự báo nói cuối tuần sẽ mưa to suốt, nên buổi dã ngoại trong rừng bị hủy.
items.explanation:
Rain is described by amount, and the fixed collocation is heavy rain (also heavy snow, heavy traffic); all weekend and the cancelled picnic show it is a lot of rain.
✗ strong — collocates with wind or currents, not rain; ✗ hard — used as an adverb ('it rained hard'), not before the noun 'rain'; ✗ big — describes the size of objects, never rain.

items.q: We ______ for the mountains at five in the morning to avoid the traffic.
items.vi: Chúng tôi lên đường đi lên núi lúc năm giờ sáng để tránh kẹt xe.
items.explanation:
Set off = start a journey; the clue is for the mountains at five in the morning, a departure towards a destination.
✗ set up — establish or arrange (a company, a tent); ✗ set about — begin doing a task (set about cleaning); ✗ set down — put something down or write it down. None of these can take 'for' + a place.

items.q: Nam: I saw Lan at the hospital yesterday. / Hoa: You ______ her — she has been in Hà Nội all week.
items.vi: Nam: Hôm qua tớ thấy Lan ở bệnh viện. / Hoa: Cậu không thể nào thấy cô ấy được — cả tuần nay cô ấy ở Hà Nội mà.
items.explanation:
Can't have + past participle = a confident deduction that something in the past was impossible; the clue is she has been in Hà Nội all week.
✗ mustn't have seen — 'must' makes positive deductions only ('must have seen'); its negative for deduction is 'can't have'; ✗ shouldn't have seen — criticism: it was wrong to see her; ✗ needn't have seen — it was unnecessary to see her.

items.q: Tickets for the island boat tour are ______ — book now or you will miss out.
items.vi: Vé tour thuyền ra đảo đang bán đắt như tôm tươi — đặt ngay kẻo hết.
items.explanation:
Sell like hot cakes = sell very quickly in large numbers; the clue is book now or you will miss out.
✗ burning the midnight oil — working or studying late into the night; ✗ raining cats and dogs — raining very heavily; ✗ going the extra mile — making more effort than is expected. Only 'selling like hot cakes' can describe tickets.

items.q: The dentist to ______ my mother goes has moved her clinic to District 3.
items.vi: Nha sĩ mà mẹ tôi hay đến khám đã chuyển phòng khám sang Quận 3.
items.explanation:
After a preposition (to) the relative pronoun must be the object form whom: 'the dentist to whom my mother goes'.
✗ who — subject form, not used directly after a preposition; ✗ whose — possessive, must be followed by a noun ('whose clinic'); ✗ which — refers to things, but the dentist is a person.

items.q: Mum was ______ to hear that it was only a cold and not the flu.
items.vi: Mẹ nhẹ cả người khi nghe đó chỉ là cảm lạnh chứ không phải cúm.
items.explanation:
Relieved = glad because a worry has gone; the clue is the good news only a cold and not the flu.
✗ relaxed — calm and not stressed, a general state rather than a reaction to news; ✗ comfortable — physically at ease or not worried, not used with 'to hear that'; ✗ peaceful — quiet and calm, describes places or moods, not a sudden feeling about news.

items.q: My uncle has suffered ______ back pain for years, so he sees a doctor every month.
items.vi: Chú tôi bị đau lưng nhiều năm nay nên tháng nào cũng đi khám bác sĩ.
items.explanation:
The verb suffer takes from when it means to have an illness or pain: suffer from back pain.
✗ of — 'suffer of' is not English (compare 'die of'); ✗ with — heard informally, but the standard pattern for an illness is 'suffer from'; ✗ by — 'by' introduces the agent of a passive verb, and 'has suffered' is active.

items.q: This time next week we ______ on a beach in Phú Quốc.
items.vi: Giờ này tuần sau chúng tôi sẽ đang nằm dài trên bãi biển ở Phú Quốc.
items.explanation:
This time next week marks an action in progress at a moment in the future, so the future continuous will be lying is needed.
✗ lie — present simple states facts or habits, not a future moment; ✗ are lying — present continuous means now or a fixed arrangement, not an action pictured in progress then; ✗ have been lying — present perfect continuous runs from the past up to now.

items.q: There's ______ time before the flight, so let's have a coffee.
items.vi: Còn một chút thời gian trước chuyến bay, nên mình đi uống cà phê đi.
items.explanation:
Time here is an uncountable noun, and the tone is positive (enough for a coffee), so a little = some.
✗ a few — only with plural countable nouns (a few minutes); ✗ many — only with plural countable nouns, so 'many time' is impossible; ✗ few — countable and negative ('almost none'), which would clash with 'let's have a coffee'.

items.q: I would like to ______ an appointment with Dr Hùng for tomorrow morning, please.
items.vi: Tôi muốn đặt lịch hẹn với bác sĩ Hùng vào sáng mai ạ.
items.explanation:
The fixed collocation is make an appointment (also make a booking, make a reservation); the clue is with Dr Hùng for tomorrow morning, i.e. arranging a time.
✗ do — used for tasks and activities (do homework), not for arranging; ✗ take — 'take an appointment' is not English (you can keep or miss one); ✗ put — needs a place ('put it in the diary') and has no collocation with 'appointment'.

items.q: Minh was ______ when the doctor told him he could not play football for a month.
items.vi: Minh thất vọng khi bác sĩ bảo cậu không được đá bóng trong một tháng.
items.explanation:
Disappointed = sad because something you hoped for will not happen; the clue is that he could not play football for a month.
✗ ashamed — feeling guilty about something bad you did, but Minh did nothing wrong; ✗ amused — finding something funny, the opposite of a reaction to bad news; ✗ grateful — thankful for help, which nobody gave here.

items.q: If I ______ you, I would see a doctor about that cough.
items.vi: Nếu tớ là cậu, tớ sẽ đi khám bác sĩ về cơn ho đó.
items.explanation:
Second conditional (imaginary present, used for advice): if + past simple, would + verb; the clue is would see in the main clause, and 'If I were you' is the fixed form.
✗ am — present simple makes a first conditional, which needs 'will', not 'would'; ✗ had been — past perfect makes a third conditional about the past (would have + p.p.); ✗ would be — 'would' belongs in the main clause, not the if-clause.

items.q: We ______ petrol halfway to the beach and had to push the car to a garage.
items.vi: Chúng tôi hết xăng giữa đường ra biển và phải đẩy xe đến tiệm sửa.
items.explanation:
Run out of = use all of something so none is left; the clue is that they had to push the car, so there was no petrol.
✗ ran into — met by chance, or crashed into; ✗ ran after — chased; ✗ ran over — hit and drove over with a vehicle. None of these can be done to petrol.

items.q: The weather in Sa Pa was terrible all week; ______, we still had a wonderful holiday.
items.vi: Thời tiết ở Sa Pa tệ suốt cả tuần; tuy nhiên, chúng tôi vẫn có một kỳ nghỉ tuyệt vời.
items.explanation:
The two halves contrast (terrible weather / still a wonderful holiday), so the linker of contrast however is needed; the word still confirms it.
✗ therefore — introduces a result, but a great holiday is not the result of bad weather; ✗ moreover — adds a point of the same kind, not an opposite one; ✗ otherwise — means 'if not', which makes no sense here.

items.q: Hoa felt ______ when she realised she had been following the wrong tour group for ten minutes.
items.vi: Hoa thấy xấu hổ khi nhận ra mình đã đi theo nhầm đoàn du lịch suốt mười phút.
items.explanation:
Embarrassed = feeling silly and uncomfortable because of a mistake others may have noticed; the clue is following the wrong tour group for ten minutes.
✗ frightened — scared of danger, but nothing dangerous happened; ✗ delighted — very pleased, the wrong reaction to a mistake; ✗ proud — pleased with an achievement, not with a silly error.

items.q: Thousands of young trees ______ in the national park every year by student volunteers.
items.vi: Hàng nghìn cây non được trồng trong vườn quốc gia mỗi năm bởi các tình nguyện viên học sinh.
items.explanation:
The trees do not plant; they are planted, and the agent follows by student volunteers, so the sentence is passive — present simple passive because every year describes a repeated fact.
✗ are planting — active continuous: the trees would be doing the planting; ✗ plant — active present simple, same problem, and 'by' would have no role; ✗ have planted — active present perfect, again making the trees the planters.

items.q: The doctor went on television to ______ about the rumours that the new vaccine was dangerous.
options: hit the nail on the head
items.vi: Bác sĩ lên truyền hình để làm rõ sự thật về những tin đồn rằng vắc-xin mới nguy hiểm.
items.explanation:
Set the record straight = give the true facts after false ones have spread; the clue is the rumours that the new vaccine was dangerous.
✗ hit the nail on the head — say exactly the right thing about a problem; ✗ turn over a new leaf — start behaving better; ✗ break the ice — say something to make strangers feel relaxed. None of these means correcting false information.

items.q: I am really looking forward to ______ my cousins in Huế this summer.
items.vi: Tớ rất mong được gặp các anh chị em họ ở Huế hè này.
items.explanation:
In look forward to, 'to' is a preposition, not an infinitive marker, so the verb after it must be a gerund: seeing.
✗ see — a bare infinitive cannot follow a preposition; ✗ to see — repeats 'to' and wrongly treats it as an infinitive marker; ✗ to seeing — doubles the preposition ('forward to to seeing').

items.q: Lan asked me ______ on holiday that summer.
items.vi: Lan hỏi tôi sẽ đi nghỉ ở đâu vào mùa hè năm đó.
items.explanation:
A reported question keeps statement word order (subject before verb) and, after the past reporting verb asked, shifts the tense back: where I was going.
✗ where was I going — question word order (verb before subject) belongs only in direct questions; ✗ where am I going — question order and no backshift; ✗ where I am going — right order, but present tense does not match 'asked' and 'that summer'.

items.q: The doctor asked me to ______ a deep breath and hold it for five seconds.
items.vi: Bác sĩ bảo tôi hít một hơi thật sâu và giữ trong năm giây.
items.explanation:
The fixed collocation is take a (deep) breath; the clue is hold it for five seconds, a single act of breathing in.
✗ make — not used with 'breath' (you make a noise or a decision); ✗ do — used for activities and tasks, not for breathing; ✗ give — you give a sigh or a shout, but not a breath.

items.q: Our tour guide stayed ______ even when the bus broke down in the rain, joking with everyone until help came.
items.vi: Hướng dẫn viên của chúng tôi vẫn vui vẻ ngay cả khi xe buýt hỏng giữa trời mưa, đùa với mọi người cho tới khi có người tới giúp.
items.explanation:
Cheerful = happy and in a good mood; the clue is joking with everyone even when the bus broke down.
✗ anxious — worried and nervous, the opposite of joking; ✗ jealous — wanting what someone else has, and there is nothing here to envy; ✗ hopeless — feeling that nothing will get better, which does not match keeping people laughing 'until help came'.

items.q: The mountains were ______ than we expected, so we bought warm jackets at the market.
items.vi: Trên núi lạnh hơn nhiều so với chúng tôi tưởng, nên chúng tôi mua áo khoác ấm ở chợ.
items.explanation:
Than after the blank needs a comparative, and far (= much) strengthens it: far colder.
✗ as cold — the equal comparison needs 'as cold as', not 'than'; ✗ far coldest — a superlative compares three or more and never goes with 'than'; ✗ more cold — 'cold' is one syllable, so it takes '-er', not 'more'.

items.q: Lan: You look exhausted! / Nam: Yes, I ______ back from Đà Lạt — the bus took eight hours.
items.vi: Lan: Trông cậu mệt quá! / Nam: Ừ, tớ vừa mới về từ Đà Lạt — xe buýt đi mất tám tiếng.
items.explanation:
Just + a recent action whose result is visible now (you look exhausted) takes the present perfect: have just come.
✗ had just come — past perfect needs an earlier past event to be 'before', but the conversation is now; ✗ just come — no auxiliary, so it is not a correct tense (the informal past would be 'just came'); ✗ am just coming — present continuous means he is still on the way, but he is already here.
